title: Fix word frequency counter to normalise case and strip punctuation
prompt: The function word_frequency(text) in starter/word_frequency.py returns a dict mapping each word to its count. It has two bugs: (1) it is case-sensitive so 'Hello' and 'hello' are counted separately, and (2) it does not strip punctuation so 'word.' and 'word' are counted separately. Fix it so that word_frequency('Hello, hello! World.') returns {'hello': 2, 'world': 1}. Words are separated by whitespace. Punctuation means any character that is not a letter or digit. An empty string returns {}. Do not edit the tests.
